title: decision-bridge: interruption-aware rollout controller with staged-failover and manual-latch
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Production rollouts occasionally collide with infrastructure interruptions (preemptible eviction, region maintenance, spot price spikes). Existing canary/AB controllers proactively gate on telemetry but do not reason about transient interruption signals that should trigger a fast, safe evacuation and staged rollback. Motivation: reduce user-visible failures during infra interruptions while preserving gradual validation semantics for model promotes. Summary: Adds a new 'decision-bridge' controller: an interruption-aware intermediary that sits between routing policy and rollout engine. It ingests interruption signals (agent heartbeats, spot-notices, region telemetry), computes a short-lived traffic-fencing plan, and coordinates a staged failover across: 1) ephemeral fallback variant (lighter quantized copy), 2) shadow capture with auto-dryrun, 3) manual-latch holdpoint for on-call intervention. The bridge supports: - graceful drain with session re-anchoring and replayable request snapshots - snapshot-based rollback plan (captures KV-cache sync points and model revision pointers) - cost-slo aware preference (prefer fallback variants when cost-slos are acceptable) - explicit holdpoints that can be bumped by SRE/owner via the Console APIs - deterministic reconciliation loop compatible with existing rollout FSMs What changed (high level): - controller/decisionbridge: new controller with policy engine, signal adapters, guard rails. - router/evacuation: routing hooks for fast fencing and session affinity resharding. - runtime/snapshot: small snapshot checkpoint API for KV cache + inflight-request capture. - console/api: holdpoint endpoints and new rollout state visualization. - e2e tests: synthetic interruption scenarios and smoke replays. Rollout plan for this PR: 1) unit & integration tests (green) 2) internal dogfood: dedicated cluster with synthetic spot-notice generator 3) staged enable on low-traffic workspace (10%) 4) progressive increase with telemetry gates and manual-latch on first 2 weeks. Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-4821) referenced - [x] unit tests for policy evaluation - [x] integration tests for session reanchoring - [x] Console UI hooks + RBAC checks - [x] e2e interruption smoke runs - [x] post-merge canary for 10% traffic - [x] runbook draft attached (SUP-914) Backwards compatibility: The decision-bridge is opt-in by rollout policy; default behavior unchanged until teams opt in. No breaking config schema changes. Security: holdpoint endpoints require role-bound permissions; audit logs added for manual latch/unlatch. Related: improves on prior shadow-promote work but focuses on interruption semantics (see ENG-2134 for staged-promote heuristics). Callouts/Tradeoffs: - We introduce a short-lived snapshot store (ephemeral in-memory + persisted checkpoints for a limited TTL) — this adds complexity for multi-revision KV sync but avoids full model checkpointing. - There is a small latency impact when forcing re-anchoring; mitigated with session borrowing window. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps fallback variants configurable and limited per-workspace to avoid cost surprises.
commits: 5 commits: 1) add decision-bridge controller scaffold and API surface; 2) implement signal adapters (preempt, spot, region-maint); 3) routing hooks + session re-anchoring; 4) snapshot checkpoint feature and persistence TTL; 5) Console endpoints, docs and runbook link

release_notes: Introduce 'Decision Bridge' interruption-aware rollout controller. Opt-in feature that coordinates graceful evacuation and staged rollback on infra interruptions. Includes Console holdpoints, snapshot-based rollback checkpoints, and routing hooks for session re-anchoring. See docs/designs/decision-bridge.md and SUP-914 runbook for operational guidance.
post_merge_tasks: 1) enable internal dogfood cluster flag for 2 weeks and monitor evacuation_active and rollback_rate metrics; 2) add a Grafana dashboard: Rollouts > DecisionBridge > Evacuation windows; 3) schedule a blameless postmortem after first large-scale preempt event with DecisionBridge enabled; 4) iterate on fallback-cost heuristics based on telemetry.
notes: This PR intentionally avoids auto-rollback on short-lived interruptions (<15s) to prevent oscillation; teams can configure sensitivity. The snapshot mechanism is not intended for long-term cold-start persistence.
